description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing and shows the expected-containers list it would create; apply adds log rotation and build-cache limits to daemon.json without disturbing the keys already there, writes a file dockerd accepts, creates the list once, from every container present, marks it not reviewed, and never rewrites it, and installs an enabled prune timer whose script never touches volumes. Before the list is reviewed, a prune with no age limit removes no container and no image. After review, a stopped container that nothing protects is first recorded in /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal (0700 root directory, 0600 file) and left alone; a run inside the grace period leaves it and says until when; a run after it (the record moved back 145 hours) removes it and drops the record. Its age counts from when it stopped: one stopped 29 days ago and one never started, created 30 days ago, are recorded; one created 30 days ago that stopped just now is not (the times are set by stopping Docker and editing config.v2.json). A recorded container added to the list, or started again, loses its record. When the record cannot be written (a read-only bind mount), no container is removed and the exit is 1, through the timer's script and through Prune now; a GRACE_HOURS under 24 written by hand is refused by the prune; and when the review is withdrawn the prune removes nothing and clears the record. Stopped containers that are on the list, have an unless-stopped policy, or are labelled tc.keep are kept with their images. Images, with a test registry on 127.0.0.1 standing in for a real one: Dangling (and a settings file with no PRUNE_IMAGES) removes the untagged image only; All also removes the tagged image pushed to the registry, printing its repo@sha256 to the journal (and that reference pulls it back), keeps the one built here and says why, and keeps tc.keep; a failing docker image ls removes no image and exits 1. On the containerd image store, where every image has a digest, All keeps every tagged image and says why. With Docker restarted under extra daemon flags each time: a --log-driver=journald daemon and a --log-opt daemon get no log-opts in daemon.json and still start; a --log-driver=json-file daemon gets them and starts with them; a stopped daemon's flags are read from docker.service and its environment file, and flags it cannot resolve skip log rotation with exit 3; a daemon.json an earlier version already broke is reported as DAEMON WILL NOT START, exit 3, unchanged, and Docker really does fail to start with it. Bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. Restarting Docker to load the new settings, and a host without Docker, are Tier 2. A container label is untrusted: one whose Compose project label carries a forged row cannot add a row or a field to the container listing, so a reviewed prune keeps the listed stopped container the forged row named, names the containers whose labels cannot be read, keeps them, and never prints the label; a new list leaves them off and says so. When docker ps fails but docker info answers (a shim on PATH), the prune prints ERROR, exits 1 and removes nothing, not even a network; Prune now exits 1; and the list is not created, exit 3. Writing daemon.json: the new file is made in the directory of the real target and renamed into place, so it keeps the mode, owner and group of the file it replaces (a 0600 file holding a fake proxy credential stays 0600 with its non-root group; a new file is 0644 root:root) and a symlinked daemon.json stays a symlink while its target changes and Docker restarts with it; a dangling symlink, or a link to a directory, is refused with exit 3 and nothing is created; after a successful Apply, a failed validation and Report mode, no .daemon.json.tc-* file is left in /etc/docker, and one left by a crashed earlier run is removed; Report mode on a host with no /etc/docker does not create it; seven changes in a row leave the newest five backups; and an immutable daemon.json makes the run exit 1 with the file byte-for-byte unchanged, no staging file and no backup.

steps.label: Record daemon.json as it was before the component
steps.run: mkdir -p /etc/docker; if [ -s /etc/docker/daemon.json ]; then cp /etc/docker/daemon.json /tmp/tc-before.json; else echo '{}' > /tmp/tc-before.json; fi; cat /tmp/tc-before.json

steps.label: Report mode
Report mode changed nothing
steps.run: test ! -e /etc/systemd/system/tc-docker-prune.timer && test ! -e /etc/tc-docker/expected-containers && { cmp -s /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json || { test ! -s /etc/docker/daemon.json && test "$(cat /tmp/tc-before.json)" = '{}'; }; }

steps.label: Apply
daemon.json carries the limits
Every key that was already there is unchanged
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; a=json.load(open('/tmp/tc-before.json')); b=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); bad=[k for k in a if b.get(k)!=a[k] and k not in ('log-opts','builder')]; print('changed:', bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

steps.label: dockerd accepts the new file
steps.run: dockerd --validate --config-file /etc/docker/daemon.json

steps.label: Prune timer enabled and scheduled
steps.run: systemctl is-enabled tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl is-active tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl list-timers tc-docker-prune.timer --no-pager

steps.label: Prune script has an age filter, never prunes volumes and never forces an image
Prune script carries one TC_PRUNE_VERSION stamp, a whole number, near the top
steps.run: f=/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune; n=$(grep -c '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=' $f); first=$(grep -n '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=' $f | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f1); echo "stamp lines: $n, first at line $first"; grep '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=' $f; [ "$n" = 1 ] && [ "$first" -le 10 ] && grep -qE '^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=[0-9]+$' $f

steps.label: The stamp equals the version in component.json
steps.run: m=Scripts/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin/component.json; [ -f "$m" ] || { echo "cannot find $m from $(pwd)"; exit 1; }; want=$(jq -r '.general.version' "$m"); have=$(sed -n 's/^TC_PRUNE_VERSION=\([0-9][0-9]*\)$/\1/p' /usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune); echo "component.json version: $want; installed stamp: $have"; [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$have" ]

steps.label: Second run changes nothing
One-off prune, before review: no containers or images touched
A run of the prune prints its version as its first line
steps.run: m=Scripts/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin/component.json; want=$(jq -r '.general.version' "$m"); out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; first=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 1); echo "first line: $first (exit $rc)"; [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ "$first" = "tc-docker-prune version $want" ]

steps.label: The prune service itself runs
steps.run: systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service && systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value

steps.label: The timer's service puts the version in the journal
steps.run: want=$(jq -r '.general.version' Scripts/docker-configure-host-maintenance-lin/component.json); journalctl --sync >/dev/null 2>&1; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service --no-pager | grep "tc-docker-prune version $want"

steps.label: Expected list created, with its header
Ignore file created with an example
Settings file carries the age, the wait and the image mode
Stopped containers: one listed, one unless-stopped, one tc.keep, one unprotected
steps.run: set -e; d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $d/bin; cp /bin/sleep /bin/true $d/bin/; for l in $(ldd /bin/sleep | grep -oE '/[^ ]+'); do mkdir -p $d$(dirname $l); cp $l $d$l; done; for t in listed policy labelled junk; do tar -C $d -c . | docker import --change "LABEL tc.test=$t" - tc-test-$t:1; done; echo name:tc-listed >> /etc/tc-docker/expected-containers; docker create --name tc-listed tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true; docker run -d --name tc-policy --restart unless-stopped tc-test-policy:1 /bin/sleep 3600; docker stop -t 1 tc-policy; docker create --name tc-labelled --label tc.keep=true tc-test-labelled:1 /bin/true; docker create --name tc-junk tc-test-junk:1 /bin/true; docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}}' | grep tc-test; docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'

steps.label: A later run never rewrites the list
The hand-added entry is still on the list
Before review: a prune with no age limit removes no container and no image, and records nothing
steps.run: sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune && systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service -n 40 --no-pager; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} survived' tc-junk; docker image inspect -f 'junk image survived' tc-test-junk:1; test ! -e /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'no pending-removal file'

steps.label: Record a review, as Update Expected Containers' Confirm reviewed does
steps.run: echo 'tc-test review' > /etc/tc-docker/reviewed && cat /etc/tc-docker/reviewed

steps.label: A later run reports the list as reviewed
After review: the first prune with no age limit, run by the timer's service, records the unprotected stopped container and removes no container
steps.run: docker inspect -f 'before: {{.Name}} present' tc-junk; sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; sleep 2; since=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'); sleep 1; systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service; systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value; journalctl --sync >/dev/null 2>&1; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service --since "$since" --no-pager -o cat; docker ps -a --format 'after: {{.Names}} {{.Status}}'
outputContains: Stopped containers recorded for removal this run (removed 144h from now if still stopped and not protected):

steps.label: The record: one line, id, key, name and time, for tc-junk only; /var/lib/tc-docker is 0700 root, the file 0600 root
steps.run: stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' /var/lib/tc-docker /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal; id=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' tc-junk); echo "tc-junk lines: $(grep -cE "^$id	name:tc-junk	tc-junk	[0-9]{10}$" /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal)"; echo "lines in all: $(grep -vc '^#' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal)"; cat /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal

steps.label: Inside the grace period: the next prune leaves it, says it is waiting and until when, and keeps the time it was first recorded
steps.run: before=$(grep 'name:tc-junk' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal | cut -f4); sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; after=$(grep 'name:tc-junk' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal | cut -f4); [ -n "$before" ] && [ "$before" = "$after" ] && echo 'first recorded: unchanged'; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} still here' tc-junk
outputContains: Stopped containers waiting to be removed:

steps.label: After the grace period (its record moved back 145 hours): the next prune removes it and drops the record; protected containers and their images stay; its unused tagged image stays, as PRUNE_IMAGES is dangling
steps.run: sed -i -E "s/^(.*	name:tc-junk	tc-junk	)[0-9]+$/\1$(( $(date +%s) - 145 * 3600 ))/" /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal; grep -v '^#' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal; sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; for c in tc-listed tc-policy tc-labelled; do docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} kept' $c; done; for i in listed policy labelled; do docker image inspect -f "image tc-test-$i kept" tc-test-$i:1; done; docker inspect tc-junk >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'tc-junk STILL HERE' || echo 'tc-junk removed'; docker image inspect -f 'junk image kept (tagged)' tc-test-junk:1; grep -q 'name:tc-junk' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'tc-junk record STILL THERE' || echo 'tc-junk record dropped'
outputContains: tagged image(s) that no container uses (PRUNE_IMAGES=dangling

steps.label: Container age: stopped 29 days ago; created 30 days ago and stopped just now; created 30 days ago and never started (Docker stopped and restarted to set the times); OLDER_THAN_HOURS=24
steps.run:
cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-age <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-age NAME=CREATED[,FINISHED] ...: stop Docker, set those containers' Created
# (and State.FinishedAt) in their config.v2.json, start Docker again. Docker sets both
# times itself and has no way to change them, so this is how a test makes a container old.
set -e
declare -A ids
for a in "$@"; do ids[${a%%=*}]=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "${a%%=*}"); done
root=$(docker info --format '{{.DockerRootDir}}')
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl stop docker.socket docker.service; else pkill -x dockerd; while pgrep -x dockerd >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done; fi
for a in "$@"; do
  n=${a%%=*}; v=${a#*=}; c=${v%%,*}; f="$root/containers/${ids[$n]}/config.v2.json"
  if [ "$v" != "$c" ]; then jq --arg c "$c" --arg f "${v#*,}" '.Created=$c | .State.FinishedAt=$f' "$f" > "$f.tc"
  else jq --arg c "$c" '.Created=$c' "$f" > "$f.tc"; fi
  mv "$f.tc" "$f"
done
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl start docker.service; else (setsid dockerd >/var/log/tc-test-dockerd.log 2>&1 </dev/null &); fi
for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
for a in "$@"; do docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} created {{.Created}}, finished {{.State.FinishedAt}}' "${a%%=*}"; done
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-age
set -e
docker run --name tc-age-stopped tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true
docker create --name tc-age-fresh tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true >/dev/null
docker create --name tc-age-never tc-test-listed:1 /bin/sleep 3600 >/dev/null
tc-test-age tc-age-stopped=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ),$(date -u -d '29 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) tc-age-fresh=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) tc-age-never=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
docker start tc-age-fresh >/dev/null; sleep 2
docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} created {{.Created}}, finished {{.State.FinishedAt}} (stopped just now)' tc-age-fresh
sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=24/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; grep OLDER_THAN_HOURS /etc/default/tc-docker-prune

steps.label: Container age counts from when it stopped: the one stopped 29 days ago and the one never started (created 30 days ago) are recorded; the one created 30 days ago but stopped just now is not
steps.run: sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; grep -q 'name:tc-age-fresh' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'tc-age-fresh: LISTED IN FILE' || echo 'tc-age-fresh: absent from the file'

steps.label: Recorded, then added to the list: the next prune keeps it and drops the record
steps.run: echo name:tc-age-stopped >> /etc/tc-docker/expected-containers; sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; grep -q 'name:tc-age-stopped' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'tc-age-stopped record STILL THERE' || echo 'tc-age-stopped record dropped'; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} kept' tc-age-stopped

steps.label: Recorded, then started again: the next prune drops the record; stopped again, it is not recorded, because it stopped just now
steps.run: grep -q 'name:tc-age-never' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'recorded before: tc-age-never'; docker start tc-age-never >/dev/null; /usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune >/dev/null; echo "prune exit $?"; grep -q 'name:tc-age-never' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'while running: tc-age-never LISTED IN FILE' || echo 'while running: tc-age-never record dropped'; docker stop -t 1 tc-age-never >/dev/null; /usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune >/dev/null; grep -q 'name:tc-age-never' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'stopped again: tc-age-never LISTED IN FILE' || echo 'stopped again: tc-age-never absent from the file'
outputContains: stopped again: tc-age-never absent from the file

steps.label: Unwritable record: tc-due recorded and its record already due (moved back 145 hours), then /var/lib/tc-docker made read-only (a read-only bind mount of itself)
steps.run: set -e; docker create --name tc-due tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true >/dev/null; sleep 2; sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; /usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune >/dev/null; sed -i -E "s/	[0-9]+$/	$(( $(date +%s) - 145 * 3600 ))/" /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal; grep -q 'name:tc-due' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'tc-due recorded, due now'; mount --bind /var/lib/tc-docker /var/lib/tc-docker; mount -o remount,bind,ro /var/lib/tc-docker; touch /var/lib/tc-docker/tc-test 2>/dev/null && echo 'read-only: NO' || echo 'read-only: yes'

steps.label: Unwritable record: the prune removes no container, says why, and exits 1
steps.run: sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} survived' tc-due
outputContains: No container was removed this run

steps.label: Unwritable record: Prune now through the component exits 1 and says why
outputContains: No container was removed this run

steps.label: Unwritable record: writable again, the same prune removes the containers whose records are due
steps.run: umount /var/lib/tc-docker; sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; docker inspect tc-due >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'tc-due STILL HERE' || echo 'tc-due removed'

steps.label: A GRACE_HOURS under 24 written into the settings file by hand is refused by the prune itself: nothing recorded or removed, exit 1
steps.run: docker create --name tc-grace tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true >/dev/null; sed -i 's/^GRACE_HOURS=.*/GRACE_HOURS=1/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; grep -q 'name:tc-grace' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'tc-grace: LISTED IN FILE' || echo 'tc-grace: absent from the file'; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} survived' tc-grace; sed -i 's/^GRACE_HOURS=.*/GRACE_HOURS=144/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; docker rm tc-grace >/dev/null
outputContains: ERROR: GRACE_HOURS in /etc/default/tc-docker-prune must be a whole number of hours, 24-8760 (it is '1')
No container is recorded or removed this run

steps.label: Review withdrawn (reviewed file deleted): the prune removes nothing and clears the record, so a later review starts every wait again
steps.run: docker create --name tc-withdrawn tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true >/dev/null; sleep 2; /usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune >/dev/null; grep -q 'name:tc-withdrawn' /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'tc-withdrawn recorded while reviewed'; mv /etc/tc-docker/reviewed /tmp/tc-reviewed; sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; test ! -e /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal && echo 'no pending-removal file now'; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} left in place' tc-withdrawn; mv /tmp/tc-reviewed /etc/tc-docker/reviewed; docker rm tc-withdrawn >/dev/null

steps.label: Images: a test registry on 127.0.0.1, and four images no container uses: untagged; tagged, built here (no registry digest); tagged and pushed to the registry (a registry digest); tagged and labelled tc.keep
Images, PRUNE_IMAGES=dangling: the untagged image goes and is named; every tagged one stays
steps.run: sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; grep PRUNE_IMAGES /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; sleep 2; out=$(/usr/local/sbin/tc-docker-prune 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "prune exit $rc"; docker image inspect $(cat /tmp/tc-untagged-id) >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'untagged image STILL HERE' || echo 'untagged image removed'; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "untagged $(cut -c8-19 /tmp/tc-untagged-id)" && echo 'untagged image named in the output'; for i in tc-test-localonly:1 localhost:5055/tc-test-pulled:1 tc-test-keepimg:1; do docker image inspect -f "$i kept" $i 2>/dev/null || echo "$i GONE"; done

steps.label: containerd image store: Docker restarted with it; there an image built here has a repo@sha256 digest too
steps.run:
set -e
cp -p /etc/docker/daemon.json /tmp/tc-store-daemon.json

steps.label: daemon.json write: seven changes in a row, each made by a run of the component
steps.run:
set -u
rm -rf /opt/tc-test-managed; rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* /etc/docker/.daemon.json.tc-*; mkdir -p /etc/docker
printf '{"debug": false}\n' > /etc/docker/daemon.json
: > /tmp/tc-bak-names
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do
  python3 -c "import json; p='/etc/docker/daemon.json'; d=json.load(open(p)); d.pop('log-opts', None); d.pop('builder', None); json.dump(d, open(p, 'w'))"
  tc-test-run-component > /tmp/tc-run.out 2>&1 || { echo "change $i failed"; cat /tmp/tc-run.out; exit 1; }
  grep -q 'daemon.json: written' /tmp/tc-run.out || { echo "change $i wrote nothing"; cat /tmp/tc-run.out; exit 1; }
  LC_ALL=C ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* | tail -n 1 >> /tmp/tc-bak-names
done
echo "newest backup after each change:"; sed 's|^/etc/docker/||' /tmp/tc-bak-names
echo "backups after seven changes: $(ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* | wc -l)"
echo "distinct backup names made: $(sort -u /tmp/tc-bak-names | wc -l)"
diff <(LC_ALL=C ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-*) <(LC_ALL=C sort /tmp/tc-bak-names | tail -n 5) && echo "the five left are the newest five"
ls -la /etc/docker
outputContains: the five left are the newest five

steps.label: daemon.json write: an immutable daemon.json (chattr +i; skipped where the filesystem cannot): exit 1, file unchanged, no staging file, no backup
steps.run:
rm -rf /opt/tc-test-managed; rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* /etc/docker/.daemon.json.tc-*; mkdir -p /etc/docker
p=/etc/docker/.tc-immutable-probe; : > $p
if ! chattr +i $p 2>/dev/null || ! lsattr $p 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | grep -q i; then
  chattr -i $p 2>/dev/null; rm -f $p
  echo "SKIPPED: this filesystem does not support chattr +i, so the immutable-file check did not run"; exit 0
fi
chattr -i $p; rm -f $p
f=/etc/docker/daemon.json
printf '%s\n' '{"proxies": {"http-proxy": "http://tc-test-user:tc-test-not-a-password@proxy.invalid:3128"}}' > $f; chmod 600 $f; chattr +i $f
sha256sum $f > /tmp/tc-imm.before
tc-test-run-component > /tmp/tc-imm.out 2>&1; rc=$?
chattr -i $f
cat /tmp/tc-imm.out
echo "component exit: $rc"
ok=0
[ "$rc" = 1 ] || { echo "WRONG: expected exit 1"; ok=1; }
grep -q "could not replace $f" /tmp/tc-imm.out || { echo "WRONG: the output does not say what failed"; ok=1; }
sha256sum -c /tmp/tc-imm.before || { echo "WRONG: daemon.json changed"; ok=1; }
n=$(ls -A /etc/docker | grep -c '^\.daemon\.json\.tc-' || true); echo "staging files left in /etc/docker: $n"; [ "$n" = 0 ] || ok=1
b=$(ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "backups left by the failed run: $b"; [ "$b" = 0 ] || ok=1
ls -la /etc/docker
exit $ok
